summary: This is the same position as leaf 14, with A14 open instead of D15. Black fills A14 and E19 at no cost (A14 can be Black's answer to White's take at A18) and then must invest at C17 or C18. So it is your 10kKO with Black needing one threat more, and besogo ranks it the same as your A-1KO+, so no grade changes. The checker's A-3KO- is wrong. It measures the ko right after White's take, while both outside liberties are still open, and counts the two free fills as approaches that each cost a threat. Its label therefore implies four threats where Black needs one, and besogo would rank it below what Black's 9th move at D15 is worth.
variations:
Moves from the leaf, White to play. Narrow area; counts are Black's threats minus White's.
1. A18 A14 pass E19 pass A19 pass C17 A18 A19! pass C18: White takes, and Black answers with the free fill A14. Black fills E19, retakes at A19 without a threat and invests at C17. White retakes at A18 without a threat. Black retakes after one threat, White's group is in atari at C18, and Black captures. Black wins with 1 threat against 0, and the count is 1 at every step.
2. A18 A14 pass E19 pass A19 pass C17 A18 pass C18: without the threat, White captures four stones and lives.
3. A18 pass C17: with both outside liberties open, White's capture is a real threat. If Black plays elsewhere, White takes the corner and lives, whatever the threats.
4. A14 B14 A18 E19: the checker's first take (after White's A14 and Black's B14 block). Black answers it with the fill E19, and the count stays 1.
5. A14 B14 A18 A19! pass C17 A18: the order of the checker's approach line, investment first. White's free retake puts Black's corner in atari while White still has E19 and A13, and Black fails even with six threats more.
6. A14 B14 A18 E19 C17: White invests while it holds the ko. Black retakes without a threat and the count is 0, so whoever invests hands the other side the direct ko.
7. A14 B14 A18 E19 A19: White connects. The C17 sacrifice and the pyramid four kill, and Black wins even with six threats fewer.

key_line: A18 A14 pass E19 pass A19 pass C17 A18 A19! pass C18
checker_part: The approach count and the direct-ko sign, through the first take. The principal line has White take at A18 right after the exchange A14 B14, while White still has two outside liberties (E19 and A13). There White's capture threatens (n_O = 0), and Black's forced-pass test needs E19, A13 and C17 (n_S = 3), so D6 prints A-3KO-. Those two fills are no approaches. After the first one, White's capture threatens nothing: with one forced Black pass, Black wins. Black can play that fill as its answer to White's take, and the count never leaves 1. This is the sente-approach weakness of design section 11 risk 2 and addendum item 6. The approach line plays the investment C17 first, an order in which Black fails even with six threats more; it works only because White is forced to pass in every round. The label count of 4 against the full count of 1 (the printed gain of -3, unlocated) shows the error. The label should be measured after the free fills, where each side needs C17 or C18 and both switch tests say yes. That gives 10kKO, as the checker prints on k120, where it reaches the right label only because its principal line happens to have White fill D15 first.
earlier_research: The only earlier verdict on this problem (k057, leaf 32: ADKO) is in another branch and is not affected. Round 2's k025 (11280 leaf 9, the same structure) found the same forced-pass over-count: the checker read the free fills and the investment as three approaches where the real count is 1, and the owner's label there is 10kKO. This leaf repeats that error at its first take. It is the same position as k120, so the two should carry the same label.
